signature.instructions:
text
TASK: VISUAL DIFF + DISCARD CLASSIFIER (STRICT JSON OUTPUT, ZERO MARKDOWN)

You will be given either:
- TWO images: image_original (Image 1 / “old”) and image_reimage (Image 2 / “new”), OR
- ONE image only.

GOAL
Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:
{"discard_image": true/false, "changes": "<string>"}

DECISION YOU MUST MAKE
A) discard_image=true ONLY when the sample is NOT useful for downstream content-change tracking because:
   1) Images are informational but identical or only trivially different, OR
   2) Both sides are non-informational (logos, icons-only, blank blocks, dividers, standalone section number/label), OR
   3) One-image case and the single image is non-informational.

B) discard_image=false when:
   1) Any meaningful informational content differs (including the entire page/diagram being different), OR
   2) One side is informational and the other is non-informational, OR
   3) Either image is unreadable/corrupt/tiny such that you cannot reliably compare (then changes="Could not infer"), OR
   4) One-image case and the single image is informational (then changes="NoMatchFound").

CRITICAL FIX (BASED ON FAILURES)
1) STYLE-ONLY CHANGES ARE TRIVIAL → DISCARD
   - Do NOT treat font weight (bold vs not bold), italics, underline, color shade, or minor formatting as meaningful if the words themselves did not change.
   - Example failure: reporting “removed bold formatting” must be treated as NO meaningful change ⇒ discard_image=true (if nothing else changed).

2) “ICON / BADGE / TIER MARKER” IS NON-INFORMATIONAL (UNLESS IT CONTAINS SUBSTANTIVE DOCUMENT CONTENT)
   - Small circular badges like “Tier 1”, small labels/icons, watermarks, tiny corner marks are considered non-informational by default.
   - Example failure: a single “Tier 1” badge in a one-image input must be discarded:
     discard_image=true and changes must state it is non-informational.

MEANINGFUL VS TRIVIAL (STRICT)
MEANINGFUL (discard_image=false; list changes you can verify):
- Any change to actual wording/numbers/dates/values.
- Any change to headings/titles/section names when the text differs.
- Diagram changes: participants/boxes/arrows/steps added/removed/renamed/reconnected.
- Entire page/diagram replaced by another page/diagram (even if they “don’t match”).
- Large cross-out/strikethrough/X invalidating content.

TRIVIAL (discard_image=true if nothing else meaningful changed):
- Layout shifts, cropping, scaling, compression artifacts, blur, minor color differences.
- Punctuation-only differences.
- Watermark/logo styling differences.
- Bold/regular changes, font changes, line thickness changes, dashed vs dotted when conveying no new information (treat as trivial unless explicitly altering meaning and you can prove it).

ABSOLUTE ANTI-HALLUCINATION RULE (MANDATORY)
Only claim a specific content change if BOTH are true:
1) You can locate the same region in both images, AND
2) You can unambiguously read/see that the content differs.

If you cannot read the exact text (or are uncertain), do NOT report that as a change.

TEXT-CHANGE REPORTING REQUIREMENT
When you report a text change, you MUST quote BOTH strings verbatim:
old (image1) vs new (image2)

If you cannot quote exactly, either:
- omit that detail, or
- only state a high-level replacement (e.g., “Entire diagram/page changed”) WITHOUT guessing.

NON-INFORMATIONAL HANDLING
Non-informational examples: only a logo/brand mark/watermark, tiny badge (“Tier 1”), blank/solid color block, simple divider line, standalone section number.

Rules:
- If BOTH images are non-informational:
  discard_image=true
  changes="Both images are non informational and contain only logos / etc.."
  (Do NOT describe logo styling differences.)
- If ONE is non-informational and the OTHER is informational:
  discard_image=false
  changes must state that only one image is informational and briefly what it contains (only what you can read/see).

ONE-IMAGE CASES
- If only one image is provided and it is non-informational:
  discard_image=true
  changes="Only one image which is non-informational and it contains logo (or watermark / blank block / single line / standalone section number / icon badge / etc.)"
- If only one image is provided and it is informational:
  discard_image=false
  changes="NoMatchFound"

UNREADABLE / CORRUPT / TOO TINY
If either image is corrupted, too tiny, or unreadable such that comparison is unreliable:
discard_image=false
changes="Could not infer"

CROSSED-OUT SPECIAL CASE
If Image 1 or Image 2 has a visible large X/strikethrough indicating invalidation:
discard_image=false
changes must start with:
"Image 1 has been crossed out" OR "Image 2 has been crossed out"
Then optionally append additional verified changes using the template below.

CHANGES FIELD FORMAT (STRICT)
1) If discarding due to no meaningful differences:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}

2) If NOT discarded and meaningful differences exist, use EXACT template:
"OVERVIEW: <brief summary> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location>: <what changed, quoting old (image1) and new (image2) text verbatim when text differs>; 2) ..."

3) If discard due to both non-informational:
Use the exact sentence given in NON-INFORMATIONAL HANDLING.

FINAL OUTPUT RULES
- Output ONLY the JSON object (no markdown, no extra keys, no reasoning).
- If style-only differences are the only differences → treat as identical → discard_image=true.
